description: YouTube Shorts. Deliberately minimal: YouTube classifies a Short on exactly two measurable properties and publishes no separate Shorts encoding specification at all.
caveats: YouTube classifies a video as a Short on two properties only: a square or vertical aspect ratio, and a duration of up to 3 minutes. Both are reported as information because they determine how the video is categorised, not whether it is accepted.

No separate Shorts codec, bitrate, file-size or minimum-resolution specification is published. Standard-upload encoding recommendations are deliberately NOT inherited here, because doing so would invent Shorts requirements that YouTube has never stated.
The two platform-wide limits that do apply — the supported container list and the 256 GB ceiling — are enforced.
The often-quoted 1080x1920 Shorts resolution is industry convention, not a published YouTube specification.

rules.explanation: The file type must be on YouTube's supported-formats list. This limit is platform-wide, not Shorts-specific.
The maximum file size you can upload is 256 GB. This limit is platform-wide, not Shorts-specific.
A video is categorised as a Short only if it has a square or vertical aspect ratio.
rules.note: This determines how YouTube categorises the video, not whether it is accepted. A wider ratio simply uploads as a long-form video.

rules.explanation: A video is categorised as a Short only if it is up to three minutes long.
rules.note: This determines categorisation, not acceptance. A longer video uploads as a long-form video.

rules.explanation: A 9:16 vertical aspect ratio is prioritised for Shorts.
rules.message_fail: This is general guidance. Any square-or-vertical ratio still classifies as a Short.

rules.note: YouTube publishes no Shorts-specific codec, bitrate, file-size or minimum-resolution specification. PreflightQC deliberately does not apply standard-upload encoding recommendations here.
